lessons.title: Non-Verbal Series: Pattern Recognition
lessons.concept: Figure/visual series questions present a sequence of shapes or diagrams that change according to a rule. You must identify the pattern (rotation, reflection, number/position of elements, shading, size changes, or combinations) and select the next figure. Since this text pack describes patterns conceptually, focus on common transformation rules.
lessons.formula: Look for: rotation (clockwise/anticlockwise by fixed angle), movement of elements, addition/removal, shading alternation, mirror images, and count changes.
lessons.worked_example: If an arrow rotates 90° clockwise in each step: up -> right -> down -> next is left. Pattern is consistent angular rotation.
mistakes: Focusing on only one element when multiple change
Missing combined rules (e.g., rotate and add a dot)
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Common Transformations
lessons.concept: Typical transformations include rotation by 45°/90°, horizontal/vertical flipping, incremental increase/decrease in sides or elements, alternating fill/shade, and positional shifts in a grid. Track each attribute separately to detect simultaneous rules.
lessons.formula: Check attributes per step: orientation, count, position, fill, size. Rule must hold across all given steps.
lessons.worked_example: A shape gains one side each step: triangle (3), square (4), pentagon (5), next hexagon (6).
mistakes: Not verifying rule on all transitions
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Systematic Solving Approach
lessons.concept: Solve by comparing consecutive figures: identify what stays same and what changes. Formulate a hypothesis and test it on every transition. For MCQs, eliminate options that violate the observed rule. When patterns combine, ensure every component follows its own consistent rule.
lessons.formula: Stepwise: observe differences -> hypothesize rule -> verify on all steps -> predict next -> match option.
lessons.worked_example: If dot moves one corner clockwise each step and shading alternates, next figure must satisfy both: correct corner and correct shading.
mistakes: Jumping to answer after one transition
